title: HLA Drug-Safety Screens, Birdshot A*29:02 and the Protective Side of B27
summary: Learn which HLA allele is screened before abacavir, carbamazepine and allopurinol, who the guidelines actually target, what a negative result does and does not exclude, and how allele-level associations work in birdshot uveitis, Behçet syndrome and protective HLA-B27.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 51 Hits 3 (HLA-B*57:01/abacavir, HLA-B*15:02/carbamazepine, HLA-B*58:01/allopurinol), 10 (birdshot HLA-A*29:02; Behçet HLA-B51) and 14 (HLA-B27 protective in HCV and HIV), checked against the FDA/DHHS/IDSA positions summarised in Ma 2010, CPIC 2018 (read via a page-fetch tool), the 2020 ACR gout guideline (read via a page-fetch tool), Biswas 2022, Somkrua 2011, Ko 2015, Campbell 2025, Mounzer 2019, Sung 2020, Herbort 2017, Kuiper 2020, Capittini 2021 and Crux 2017. Five reviewer statements are qualified by the sources and carry accuracy flags. The reviewer’s Number Vault (table1) and Figure 51 are not taught here because this lesson covers only part of each. Not taught: the genetics of HLA typing methods, ankylosing spondylitis itself, celiac DQ2/DQ8, complement and HFE content of this chapter.

objectives: Match abacavir, carbamazepine and allopurinol to the HLA allele screened before each, and state which patient groups the guidelines target.
Explain what a negative HLA drug-safety screen does and does not exclude.
Interpret allele-level disease associations of very different strength, from HLA-A*29:02 in birdshot uveitis to HLA-B51 in Behçet syndrome and protective HLA-B27.

scenes.title: Three drugs, three alleles, one morning
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: three HLA typing requests reach the laboratory in one morning — (1) HIV clinic, adult about to start abacavir; (2) neurology, a carbamazepine-naive patient of Thai ancestry; (3) rheumatology, a Han Chinese patient about to start allopurinol. Each form asks only for “HLA typing”. Question token: “Which allele, and what does a negative result actually buy?”

cues.text: Three HLA requests arrive in one morning. An adult about to start abacavir. A carbamazepine-naive patient of Thai ancestry. A patient of Han Chinese descent about to start allopurinol.
Every form says only “HLA typing”. Each drug has its own allele, and ordering the wrong one wastes the only chance to prevent the reaction.
And once the result is negative, what has the test actually bought the patient?

props.label: Which allele — and what does a negative buy?

scenes.title: Three drug–allele pairs
scenes.altText: Schematic: three cards, one per drug-allele pair. Abacavir and HLA-B*57:01 — hypersensitivity affects 5–8% of patients in the first 6 weeks; the FDA prescribing information carries a recommendation to screen for HLA-B*57:01 before starting, and carriers should not be given the drug. Carbamazepine and HLA-B*15:02 — the label carries a boxed warning about Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis in carriers; the allele is common in several Asian populations and rare in European ones. Allopurinol and HLA-B*58:01 — the 2020 ACR gout guideline conditionally recommends testing in patients of Southeast Asian descent (Han Chinese, Korean, Thai) and African American patients, and conditionally recommends against testing everyone else. A fourth card holds the effect sizes.

cues.text: Abacavir pairs with HLA-B star 57 colon 01. Hypersensitivity hits five to eight percent of patients, usually in the first six weeks, and the prescribing information recommends screening before the first dose. A carrier should not receive the drug.

Carbamazepine pairs with HLA-B star 15 colon 02. The label carries a boxed warning about Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis in carriers. The allele is common in several Asian populations and rare in European ones.

Allopurinol pairs with HLA-B star 58 colon 01. The 2020 American College of Rheumatology gout guideline conditionally recommends testing patients of Southeast Asian descent and African American patients, and conditionally recommends against testing everyone else.

The effect sizes are large. Pooled odds ratios run about twenty-six for carbamazepine and B star 15 colon 02, and from seventy-nine to ninety-seven for allopurinol and B star 58 colon 01 depending on the control group.

scenes.title: What screening buys — and what it misses
scenes.altText: Two blocks. Block one, screening works: in the PREDICT-1 randomised study of 1956 patients, immunologically confirmed abacavir hypersensitivity was 2.7% in the control arm and 0% in the screened arm; in a Taiwanese national prospective cohort of 2910 people, 19.6% tested HLA-B*58:01 positive and were steered to another drug, and no severe cutaneous adverse reaction occurred in the screened-negative patients who took allopurinol, against seven expected from historical incidence; in Singapore, after HLA-B*15:02 genotyping became standard of care for new patients of Asian ancestry, carbamazepine-associated Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis reports fell by 92%. Block two, the residual risk: HLA-B*15:02 predicts SJS/TEN, while HLA-A*31:01 is the allele tied to DRESS and maculopapular exanthema as well as SJS/TEN, so a negative B*15:02 does not cover every carbamazepine reaction; HLA-B*58:01 was absent in more than a third of US allopurinol severe-reaction cases; pooled abacavir data give a positive predictive value of 82% and a negative predictive value of 85% against clinically diagnosed reactions.

cues.text: Screening works. In the PREDICT-1 randomised study, confirmed abacavir hypersensitivity was two point seven percent without screening and zero percent with it. In a Taiwanese national cohort, nearly twenty percent tested B star 58 colon 01 positive and were steered elsewhere, and no severe reaction occurred among those screened negative.

In Singapore, once B star 15 colon 02 genotyping became standard of care for new patients of Asian ancestry, carbamazepine-associated Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis reports fell by ninety-two percent.

Now the catch. B star 15 colon 02 predicts Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis. A different allele, A star 31 colon 01, carries the risk of drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms and of maculopapular rash, so a negative B star 15 colon 02 does not cover every carbamazepine reaction.

And B star 58 colon 01 was absent in more than a third of United States allopurinol severe-reaction cases, while pooled abacavir figures give a positive predictive value of eighty-two percent and a negative predictive value of eighty-five percent against clinically diagnosed reactions.

props.label: Policy + subsidy changed practice, not just guidance
B*58:01 absent in >1/3 of US cases

scenes.title: Allele-level thinking beyond drugs
scenes.altText: Schematic: two disease cards and the hook answers. Birdshot retinochoroiditis (HLA-A29 uveitis) — the strongest known HLA-disease association, odds ratio 157.5 with HLA-A*29:02, and HLA-A29 positivity is a required diagnostic criterion in the proposed criteria set; with PCR-based typing the association approaches 100% rather than the older “over 95%” figure from antibody methods. But HLA-A29 is carried by roughly 5–10% of Western Europeans while the disease is rare, and HLA-A*29:02 is also common in populations where birdshot is not reported, so the allele is necessary rather than sufficient. Behçet syndrome — a 2021 global meta-analysis of 31 case-control studies found HLA-B51 the strongest marker, pooled odds ratio 5.81. Hook answers: abacavir → B*57:01; carbamazepine → B*15:02; allopurinol → B*58:01.

cues.text: The same allele-level thinking runs outside pharmacogenomics. Birdshot retinochoroiditis, now often called HLA-A29 uveitis, carries the strongest known association of any disease with a tissue antigen: an odds ratio of about one hundred fifty-eight with A star 29 colon 02.

With antibody typing the figure was quoted as over ninety-five percent of patients; with PCR typing it approaches one hundred percent, and A29 positivity is a required criterion in the proposed diagnostic set. Yet around five to ten percent of Western Europeans carry A29 and almost none get the disease.

Behçet syndrome sits at the other end of the scale. A global meta-analysis of thirty-one case-control studies put the pooled odds ratio for HLA-B51 at about five point eight — real, reproducible, and far too weak to diagnose anyone.
Back to the three requests. Abacavir takes B star 57 colon 01, carbamazepine takes B star 15 colon 02, and allopurinol takes B star 58 colon 01.

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “A negative HLA-B*57:01 makes abacavir safe” (✓ pooled negative predictive value 85% against clinically diagnosed reactions — lower risk, not no risk); “Screen HLA-B*58:01 in everyone before allopurinol” (✓ the 2020 ACR guideline conditionally recommends testing only in Southeast Asian descent and African American patients, and conditionally against in all others); “HLA-B27 is purely a disease allele” (✓ B*27 is enriched in HIV controllers and is associated with spontaneous hepatitis C clearance).

cues.text: Trap one: a negative B star 57 colon 01 makes abacavir safe. No. Against clinically diagnosed reactions the pooled negative predictive value is about eighty-five percent. Lower risk, not no risk.

Trap two: screen everyone for B star 58 colon 01 before allopurinol. No. The guideline recommends testing only patients of Southeast Asian descent and African American patients, and recommends against testing the rest.
Trap three: HLA-B27 is purely a disease allele. No. The same allele is enriched in people who control HIV without treatment and is linked to spontaneous clearance of hepatitis C.

props.title: ✗ “Screen everyone for B*58:01.”
lines: ✓ SE Asian descent + African American only

props.title: ✗ “B27 only ever harms.”

cues.text: Memory aid: fifty-seven for the HIV pill, fifteen for the seizure pill, fifty-eight for the gout pill. Abacavir, carbamazepine, allopurinol — three numbers in one chant.

Where it breaks: the chant hides who gets tested and what a negative means. Carbamazepine also needs A star 31 colon 01 for rash and DRESS, the allopurinol test is only recommended for specific ancestry groups, and no negative result removes the need to watch the patient.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “Abacavir → B*57:01 · carbamazepine → B*15:02 · allopurinol → B*58:01”, “A negative lowers risk, it does not remove it”.

cues.text: Screen HLA-B star 57 colon 01 before abacavir, HLA-B star 15 colon 02 before carbamazepine in patients of Asian ancestry, and HLA-B star 58 colon 01 before allopurinol in patients of Southeast Asian descent or African American patients, remembering that a negative result lowers risk rather than removing it.

props.label: Abacavir → B*57:01 · carbamazepine → B*15:02 · allopurinol → B*58:01
A negative lowers risk — it does not remove it

explanation.what: Plain language: a few HLA alleles make specific drugs dangerous, so the allele is typed before the first dose and carriers get a different drug. Other HLA alleles mark diseases, and a few of the same alleles actually help against viruses. Scientific terms: HLA-B*57:01, HLA-B*15:02, HLA-A*31:01, HLA-B*58:01, HLA-A*29:02, HLA-B51, HLA-B*27, hypersensitivity reaction (HSR), Stevens-Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis (SJS/TEN), drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS), maculopapular exanthema (MPE), severe cutaneous adverse reaction (SCAR), odds ratio, negative predictive value.
explanation.why: These reactions are rare but severe and have no treatment other than stopping the drug, so prevention has to happen before the first dose. Because allele frequencies differ between ancestry groups, testing everyone is not cost-effective and the guidelines target the groups in which the allele is common.
explanation.measure: Abacavir: hypersensitivity in 5–8%, first 6 weeks; the prescribing information recommends HLA-B*57:01 screening; pooled PPV 82% and NPV 85% against clinically diagnosed reactions. Carbamazepine: boxed warning for SJS/TEN in HLA-B*15:02 carriers; pooled OR ≈ 26 for SJS/TEN; HLA-A*31:01 (pooled OR ≈ 5.9) covers DRESS and MPE as well. Allopurinol: HLA-B*58:01 pooled OR 79–97; ACR 2020 conditionally recommends testing in Southeast Asian descent (Han Chinese, Korean, Thai; carriage 7.4%) and African American patients (3.8%), conditionally against in others (0.7% in white and Hispanic patients).
explanation.differs: Drug-safety screening (act before the first dose, allele-specific, ancestry-targeted) vs disease association (HLA-A*29:02 in birdshot, OR ≈ 157.5, part of the diagnostic criteria) vs weak marker (HLA-B51 in Behçet, pooled OR ≈ 5.81) vs protective allele (HLA-B*27 and HLA-B*57 enriched in HIV controllers and linked to hepatitis C clearance).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: match drug to allele; decide whether a patient qualifies for HLA-B*58:01 testing; interpret a negative screen; recognise that HLA-B27 can be protective in viral infection.

mnemonic.text: “57 for the HIV pill, 15 for the seizure pill, 58 for the gout pill.” Abacavir takes HLA-B*57:01, carbamazepine takes HLA-B*15:02, allopurinol takes HLA-B*58:01.
mnemonic.explanation: Three drug–allele pairs reduced to three numbers in one chant.
mnemonic.limitation: The chant hides who is tested and what a negative means: carbamazepine risk also runs through HLA-A*31:01 (DRESS and maculopapular rash), HLA-B*58:01 testing is recommended only for specific ancestry groups, and no negative screen removes the need for clinical monitoring.

analogyLimitations: Cards are schematic; no clinical images are used.
Odds ratios and predictive values are pooled estimates that vary with population and case definition.
takeaway: Screen HLA-B*57:01 before abacavir, HLA-B*15:02 before carbamazepine in patients of Asian ancestry, and HLA-B*58:01 before allopurinol in patients of Southeast Asian descent or African American patients, remembering that a negative result lowers risk rather than removing it.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old African American patient with gout is about to start allopurinol. Under the 2020 American College of Rheumatology gout guideline, what is recommended before the first dose?

options.rationale: Correct. The guideline conditionally recommends HLA-B*58:01 testing in patients of Southeast Asian descent and in African American patients, who have a higher prevalence of the allele.
Incorrect. HLA-B*57:01 is the abacavir allele, not the allopurinol allele.

options.text: No HLA testing, because the guideline recommends against testing in every group
options.rationale: Incorrect. The guideline recommends against testing only in groups other than Southeast Asian descent and African American patients.

options.text: HLA-B*15:02 testing because of the risk of Stevens-Johnson syndrome
options.rationale: Incorrect. HLA-B*15:02 is screened before carbamazepine, not allopurinol.

questions.stem: A carbamazepine-naive patient tests negative for HLA-B*15:02. What does this result allow you to say?

options.text: The risk of Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis is reduced, but other carbamazepine reactions such as DRESS and maculopapular rash are not excluded
options.rationale: Correct. HLA-B*15:02 predicts SJS/TEN; DRESS and maculopapular exanthema are associated with HLA-A*31:01, so clinical monitoring continues.

options.text: Carbamazepine can be given without any further monitoring
options.rationale: Incorrect. Not all carbamazepine cutaneous reactions are attributable to these alleles, so all patients are still monitored.

options.text: The patient has no HLA-associated drug risk at all
options.rationale: Incorrect. HLA-A*31:01 carries risk of DRESS, maculopapular exanthema and SJS/TEN and is a separate test.
Incorrect. A negative result removes the HLA-B*15:02 contraindication rather than creating one.

questions.stem: Which statement about HLA-B27 is supported by studies of viral infection?

options.text: It is enriched among people who control HIV and is associated with spontaneous hepatitis C clearance
options.rationale: Correct. HLA-B*27 and HLA-B*57 are enriched in HIV controllers, and both are associated with spontaneous clearance of hepatitis C.
Incorrect. Alleles such as HLA-B*08 and HLA-B*35 are linked to worse HIV outcome; B*27 is on the protective side.

options.text: It has no effect on viral infection because it is purely an autoimmunity allele
options.rationale: Incorrect. The same allele has both an autoimmune association and a documented antiviral advantage.

options.text: It protects against every hepatitis C genotype equally
options.rationale: Incorrect. The protective hepatitis C effect is tied to a conserved NS5B epitope present in genotype 1, which other genotypes lack.

claims.text: Abacavir hypersensitivity in 5–8% within 6 weeks; HLA-B*57:01 screening recommended in the prescribing information and by DHHS/IDSA; pooled PPV 82%, NPV 85%; PREDICT-1 2.7% vs 0%.
HLA-B*15:02 boxed warning for carbamazepine SJS/TEN; pooled OR ≈ 26; HLA-A*31:01 adds DRESS and maculopapular exanthema at OR ≈ 5.9; a negative B*15:02 does not cover all reactions.
Singapore made HLA-B*15:02 genotyping standard of care for new patients of Asian ancestry in 2013; carbamazepine-associated SJS/TEN reports fell 92%.

HLA-B*58:01 and allopurinol SJS/TEN pooled OR 79–97; ACR 2020 conditionally recommends testing in Southeast Asian descent and African American patients only; prospective screening in Taiwan prevented expected SCARs; the allele was absent in more than a third of US SCAR cases.

Birdshot retinochoroiditis and HLA-A*29:02: OR ≈ 157.5, approaching 100% of patients with PCR typing, A29 a required diagnostic criterion; allele common in Western Europeans while the disease is rare.
HLA-B51 is the strongest HLA marker of Behçet syndrome, pooled OR ≈ 5.81 across 31 case-control studies.
HLA-B*27 (with HLA-B*57) is enriched in HIV controllers and associated with spontaneous hepatitis C clearance; the hepatitis C effect is tied to a conserved NS5B epitope present in genotype 1.
Reviewer claim that HLA-A*29:01 is “predominant in Asians” and exempt from birdshot risk.
claims.note: Not taught. The sources read attribute risk to HLA-A*29:02 as the common European A29 allele and do not describe A*29:01 as an Asian-predominant exempt allele; see accuracy flag f-a2902-context.

claims.text: Reviewer’s Behçet OR of 5.9 from a meta-analysis of 4800 cases and >16,000 controls.
claims.note: That specific meta-analysis was not read; the lesson teaches the independently published pooled OR 5.81 from Capittini 2021 instead.

“57 for the HIV pill, 15 for the seizure pill, 58 for the gout pill.”

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 51 Hit 3 presents HLA-B*57:01 screening as a clean preventive test, and the imported simulator states its negative predictive value is 100%. Ma 2010 reports pooled PPV 82% (71–90%) and NPV 85% (81–88%) against clinically diagnosed hypersensitivity; the 94–100% sensitivity figure applies only to patch-test-confirmed reactions (register flag rv-hla-b5701-npv-limits).

Ch. 51 Hit 3 names only HLA-B*15:02 for carbamazepine. CPIC 2018 also recommends avoiding carbamazepine in carbamazepine-naive HLA-A*31:01 carriers, an allele that predicts DRESS and maculopapular exanthema as well as SJS/TEN and is not restricted to Asian ancestry (register flag rv-hla-cbz-a3101-missing).

Ch. 51 Hit 3 implies HLA-B*58:01 testing identifies the patients at risk from allopurinol. Campbell 2025 found the allele absent in more than a third of US allopurinol severe-reaction cases and calls it an incomplete indicator of risk (register flag rv-hla-b5801-residual-risk).

Ch. 51 Hit 10 states that >95% of birdshot patients carry HLA-A*29:02 and that A*29:01, “predominant in Asians”, is exempt. Herbort 2017 reports the association approaches 100% with PCR typing (the >95% figure came from antibody methods), and Kuiper 2020 shows HLA-A*29:02 itself is common in populations where birdshot is not reported, so allele subtype alone does not explain the restriction (register flag rv-hla-a2902-birdshot-context).

Ch. 51 Hit 14 states that HLA-B27 is protective in HCV and HIV without qualification. Crux 2017 ties the hepatitis C protection to a conserved NS5B 2841–2849 epitope present in genotype 1 and absent from other genotypes (register flag rv-hla-b27-hcv-genotype).

The screening recommendations taught here are US and Singapore instruments (FDA prescribing information, CPIC, ACR, Singapore HSA). Philippine regulatory requirements for pre-prescription HLA typing were not located in an open source and are not covered (register flag rv-hla-drug-screening-us-only).
